rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and acknowledges image limitations, but it is somewhat equivocal about stage (3 vs early 4), comments on collapse/handling effects without certainty, and gives limited concrete zona assessment.

Integrates key factors well: young age, prior live birth, prior ectopic/biochemical losses, modest oocyte yield, FSH, sperm parameters, BMI, endometrium, and lifestyle; links these to prognosis, though some interactions remain somewhat generic.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with probability estimates tied to embryo quality and patient history. Minor inconsistency remains around grading terminology and fresh/frozen assumptions, but conclusions are broadly supported.

Recommendations are largely guideline-concordant: single embryo transfer, luteal support, early monitoring after prior ectopic, and selective rather than routine PGT-A at age 28. Small deviations include speculative comments about reserve and some broad adjunct suggestions.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and future workup, including SET, luteal support, early beta-hCG/ultrasound, and evaluation for tubal/uterine factors if unsuccessful. Useful, though not highly detailed on protocol-level specifics.
